text: 🏦 Nafin, Mexico's development bank, backs Olinia's industrialization. "Making Mexico a scientific, technological and productive power is not just an aspiration — it is a task we are already building." — Carlos Torres Rosas, director of Nacional Financiera Nafin will accompany Olinia in selecting the industrial partners that take it from design to production. The project aligns with Plan México: produce more at home, strengthen the domestic market.

🇲🇽 "Olinia proved Mexico can design technology for its own needs." "Olinia demonstrated that in Mexico we can design and develop technological products for our own needs. The next step: a company that can build, distribute and sell them across the country." — Roberto Capuano, Olinia project director Timeline: call published late September, letters of intent in October, offers in November, round closes in December — targeting Olinia 1 production by summer 2027.

🏭 Mexico opens a public call to build Olinia — majority Mexican capital required. "The goal is very clear: a solid company, with majority Mexican capital, able to produce these vehicles in our country." — Rosaura Ruiz, Secretary of Science (Secihti) With Nacional Financiera, the government will launch a public, competitive call to select strategic manufacturing partners. National and foreign companies compete on equal terms — rules public from day one.

🔌 Plugs into any outlet. Costs 4x less to run than a cargo van. "Operating Olinia costs four times less than a light cargo vehicle — and a third of what it costs to operate a motocarro." — Roberto Capuano, Olinia project director A new category is born: compact electric minivehicles for local, low-speed trips. Not motorcycles, not cars. The Economy Secretariat is building regulatory certainty for the segment.
banner: OLINIA: 4X CHEAPER TO RUN THAN A VAN

text: 🛻 650 kg payload, 120+ km range, 12 crates. Price: around 150,000 pesos. "Today we show you — and Mexico — Olinia Carga: the minicar that carries big." — Roberto Capuano, Olinia project director Fits 12 huacales — Mexico's standard produce crates — with drop-side panels on all sides and a lower trunk where a gas engine would sit. Olinia 1 goes on sale summer 2027; Carga, late 2027.

🚗⚡ Olinia Carga: Mexico's second homegrown mini-EV, unveiled at the National Palace. "The goal is to promote mini-electromobility in our country — vehicles designed for the characteristics of Mexico, with the best engineering developed by public universities." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, presenting Olinia Carga 70 engineers and specialists from TecNM, IPN, UNAM and state universities develop Olinia in Puebla. Today: the cargo model — and the plan to turn the project into a company through mixed public-private investment.

🇲🇽📊 <u>MEXICO'S ECONOMY: +2.7% ANNUAL IN JULY</u>

No recession here. INEGI's IOAE nowcast has Mexico's economy growing 2.7% annually in July, accelerating from 2.0% in June, with both industry and services expanding, El Economista reports. Monthly growth was a modest 0.1% — on top of a 1.5% quarterly GDP expansion in Q2, in the middle of Washington's tariff war. Private analysts keep forecasting 1.2% for 2026; the economy keeps beating their obituaries.
